mixed_density_prob_copula() for many means under one covariance

Source: R/conditionalDesignCopula.R
mixed_density_copula_prep.Rd

Factors the parts of mixed_density_prob_copula() that depend only on the covariance – the inverse and log-determinant of the continuous block, and the conditional covariance of the ordinal block – once, and returns a function that evaluates the log density for many means, observed values and threshold bounds at once (one per column), e.g. a patient's density at every integration grid point.

The ordinal box probability is computed by adaptive Gauss-Hermite quadrature (box_prob_quadrature()) when the patient's ordinal rows involve a single ordinal random effect (e.g. one ordinal biomarker with a random intercept). Given the continuous values, the ordinal latent scores then have covariance \(l l^T + I\), \(l l^T\) from the random effect and \(I\) from the latent residuals, so they are independent given the random effect, and the probability is a one-dimensional integral of a product of univariate normal probabilities. It used to be computed by mvtnorm::pmvnorm()'s Monte Carlo algorithm, which dominated the run time of every prediction with an ordinal biomarker, differed between runs (relative error around \(10^{-4}\)), and needed set.seed() to be reproducible. With two or more ordinal random effects pmvnorm() is still used: a product quadrature grid then needs so many nodes to match its accuracy (a random intercept with a large variance makes the integrand lopsided) that it is no faster. It is also used when the covariance does not have this structure, and when box = "pmvnorm".

Usage

mixed_density_copula_prep(
  Sigma_all,
  cc_idx,
  oo_idx,
  box = c("quadrature", "pmvnorm")
)

Arguments

Sigma_all

Full stacked covariance matrix for this patient (as returned by build_conditional_design_copula()).

cc_idx, oo_idx

Integer index vectors (into the stacked row order) of the continuous- and ordinal-marker rows respectively.

box

"quadrature" (default) or "pmvnorm".

Value

A function (mu_full, y_all_vec, alpha_lower_vec, alpha_upper_vec) returning the log densities. mu_full is a vector or a matrix with one column per evaluation; the other three may be vectors (the same for every column) or matrices of the same shape.
